name: SDAPT
title: Domain Adaptive Pretraining in Split Learning for Vision Foundation Models
summary: SDAPT adapts a shared vision foundation model to unlabeled domain images. Frozen client layers keep local computation light; server-side self-distillation learns a common representation, then each client trains its own task head.

figure.alt: Frozen client layers upload image features to a shared self-distillation server. The adapted frozen encoder returns representations for local task heads.
figure.caption: Adapt a shared backbone with unlabeled images, then train task-specific heads locally.

method.title: Extract local features
method.text: Frozen client layers process two global and eight local image crops. Raw images remain local; CLS and patch tokens are uploaded.

method.title: Adapt on the server
method.text: Combine all client features into one batch. Train the student with DINO, iBOT and KoLeo, update an EMA teacher, and return no gradients to frozen clients.

method.title: Specialize locally
method.text: Freeze the adapted teacher backbone. Return representations to each client, which trains a task-specific head using its own labels.

findings.title: Label-efficient adaptation
findings.text: SDAPT gains 7.4 percentage points on average across nine few-shot settings spanning three domains.

findings.title: Budget-dependent trade-offs
findings.text: MocoSFL is competitive at low adaptation budgets; SDAPT benefits more from additional data and communication.

findings.title: Shared representations, distinct tasks
findings.text: One CheXpert-adapted backbone improves average AUROC from 77.41 to 80.68 across eight labels.

abstract: Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) support tasks with limited labeled data, although their performance can decline in specialized domains. Domain-Adaptive Pretraining (DAPT) can address this limitation by adapting their representations using unlabeled in-domain images; yet these often are privacy-sensitive and distributed across resource-constrained devices. Split Learning (SL) addresses these constraints by offloading computation to a server while keeping raw images local. Existing SL methods, however, explore self-supervised training from scratch, leaving collaborative DAPT of VFMs underexplored. For this, we propose SDAPT, which performs server-side DAPT with LoRA adapters using features from frozen client layers, then trains task-specific heads on the frozen adapted VFM, keeping images and labels local. Across 3 domains, and diverse few-shot settings, we observe mean gains of 7.4 pp over direct fine-tuning, while adapting once on unlabeled domain data yields shared representations that improve performance across multiple downstream tasks.
